questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Egypt is a vast, exciting and dynamic place that I wanted to experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The only bad things that I can think of are that Egypt can be a rough place to live in.

And then it is also frustrating that there are so many things to do but you have to dedicate most of your time to the studies.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good assistance from the IPSO office at AUC.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Rely on your network - ask previous students that have been on exchange at the same destination. And always go see the apartment in real life. And ask about rules like visits, visits of people from the opposite gender and so on.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite stressful, but AUC has a really nice method where you can go to as many courses as you want the first week and see how the courses and the professor seem and then decide afterwards. This way, you can try a lot of things and it is also really helpful to see how the professor teaches before you decide.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The IPSO office offered help about logistics and some tips about the different courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted. However, time conflicting courses can be a problem.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Excellent teachers and academic programs! The only lacking thing could be engaging classmates.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses at level 3000 and level 4000, which gave me a lot more time compared to a 5000 level course, but also put me in a class with very young students whose level was not that high always.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More tests, less trust. More essays, which can be annoying but also makes you learn

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: This was the mandatory exchange (not Erasmus), which I did in Alexandria and took arabic-courses.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
History of Zionism and Modern Judaism
Political Economy of the Global South
Selected Topics (arabic MSA)
History of the city of Cairo

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. I also recommend taking different courses to try different things when you have the opportunity to have 4 courses.

An apartment where the landlord rip you off.

questions.answer:
Food was much less expensive

Some things like for example clothes can be the same price.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Very nice sports facilities and different clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the French Institute or other cultural institutes (the german, the dutch - zawya cinema) to watch movies and to go to concerts.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See as many places as you can. Alexandria is a must.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The cultural difference is big, but the transition was not hard (was probably a lot easier as a man)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just try and speak with everyone and speak as much as you can - even if your Arabic is not that good, just keep trying.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Traffic, congestion, noise, pollution can be hard things.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Egyptians are the funniest and warmest people on earth.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Talk as much Arabic as you can, don't spend all your time on studies, and visit as many places as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing another culture and trying to live in also an economically very different country

questions.answer: Yes
